solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Clean bottom lip, following medic

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so the piece printed first in the clue goes second in the answer

parts.note: DR is the usual abbreviation for doctor
a lip is the rim or brink of something

explanation.surface: A doctor gives instructions for cleaning a patient's lower lip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clean bottom lip' reads as one phrase about a mouth, but the definition stops at 'bottom': DR + EDGE gives DREDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge is to scoop mud and silt from the bed of a river or harbour, clearing out its floor.

clue.text: Traveller on beach in shade, European plagued by insects

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
E is the standard abbreviation for European
full of bugs

explanation.surface: A European tourist sits in the shade on the sand, pestered by flies.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites you to picture a person, but the traveller is a vehicle: DUN + E + BUGGY makes DUNE BUGGY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dune buggy is a light open car with big tyres built for driving over sand.

clue.text: Is one's time up in Labour now, then?

definitions.meaning: the surface asks whether a politician's career is finished; the setter means a prison sentence that has been fully served
the surface suggests the Labour Party; read it as someone formerly Conservative who has crossed the floor, with a nod to hard labour in prison

explanation.surface: A political pundit wonders whether a party's time in power is over now.
explanation.walkthrough: EX-CON works twice: a former convict whose time is up, and an ex-Conservative (Con is the party's abbreviation) who has defected to Labour, Britain's main centre-left party.
explanation.definitionFit: A former prisoner who has served the sentence is an ex-convict; someone who left the Tories is literally a former Con.

clue.text: After a couple of drinks, well game!

indicators.note: coming after means following behind, so the later piece is tacked on at the end of the answer

parts.note: two spirits, one after the other
both are exclamations of mild surprise

explanation.surface: Someone who has had two drinks declares themselves up for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like the adjective meaning willing, but it is the definition as a noun. GIN + RUM + MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin rummy is a two-player card game, a quick variant of rummy where you knock to end a hand.

clue.text: Warmer place in Wales

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a knitted garment that keeps you warm
second meaning: a town on the west coast of Wales

explanation.walkthrough: 'Warmer' looks like a comparative adjective about the weather, but it is a noun: something that warms you. Cardigan is a town on Cardigan Bay in west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted jacket buttoned down the front, worn to keep warm; the town gives its name to the bay.

clue.text: Protein-rich food source, a new green bean to eat beginning to disagree with us

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the last piece is simply added on at the end
eating takes something inside, so one piece swallows another
something made new is remade, so these letters come out in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vegetarian recommends a new green bean as a protein source, even though it may not agree with your stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds vegetarian, but the protein comes from beef. The bean is not a definition; it is raw letters, and the D is eaten partway through the rearranged result.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aberdeen Angus is a Scottish breed of beef cattle, so it is literally a source of protein-rich meat.

clue.text: Lift not working, service called in, so mended

indicators.note: someone called in is brought inside, so one piece is placed within the other
in a down entry, lifting something raises it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a machine that has stopped working is dead
the Royal Navy, known as the Senior Service

explanation.surface: The lift broke down, so the service engineer was called in and repaired it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like the broken elevator, but in a down answer it is the instruction to read upwards. The Royal Navy is called the Senior Service, a stock crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To darn is to repair a hole in knitted cloth by weaving thread across it, so socks that were darned were mended.

clue.text: Slides sliding off, it separates

indicators.note: a thing that separates sits between parts, splitting the other piece in two
something gone off has gone bad, so these letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange
'it' is a crossword stand-in for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Someone watching photo slides slip out of a projector notes that they fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slides' suggests photographs or playground rides, but it is the musical sense. 'It' meaning sex appeal is an old crossword convention from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a rapid slide through a run of musical notes; glissandi is the Italian plural.

clue.text: Terminals in nine ready, five plugs wired

indicators.note: terminals are end points, so only the outermost letters of each word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters

indicators.note: a plug fills a gap, so this piece is pushed into the middle of the other

parts.note: the first and last letters
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: An electrician checks that the terminals are ready and five plugs have been wired.
explanation.walkthrough: The electrical surface makes 'wired' look like a word about cables; it is the definition, slang for jittery. NE + RY with V plugged in gives NERVY.
explanation.definitionFit: Wired is slang for tense and jumpy, as if over-stimulated, and nervy means anxious and on edge.

clue.text: Lack of honesty old city avoided? That's not possible

parts.note: a lack of something is no amount of it

indicators.note: what is avoided is kept out, so these letters are dropped from the phrase

parts.note: candour is frankness and truthfulness
Ur, the ancient Mesopotamian city, is the crossword's favourite old city; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of dishonesty for avoiding a visit to an ancient city, and protests that it could not be done.
explanation.walkthrough: NO CANDOUR loses the UR at its end. Ur of the Chaldees is the stock 'old city' in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is a colloquial refusal meaning the request cannot be carried out, a flat statement of impossibility.

clue.text: Cocky model on cover, if with slight flaw

indicators.note: with means accompanied by, so the last piece is added on at the end
to model is to shape, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
a small dent is a minor blemish

explanation.surface: A self-assured model appears on a magazine cover despite a small blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like the cocky person on the cover; it is the instruction to reshape ON COVER IF, which then takes DENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocky means brashly sure of oneself, and overconfident describes trusting your own abilities more than is justified.

clue.text: Organ that is held in each hand, further back

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

indicators.note: something held in is gripped inside, so one piece sits between the letters of another

parts.note: left and right, one letter for each hand
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: An organ, or some object, is grasped in both hands and held further back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the instrument, but it is the body part. The two hands are L and R, holding IE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Further back in time means at a previous point, which is what earlier describes.

clue.text: Language family don't allow, excessively outspoken

parts.note: to ban is to forbid

indicators.note: speaking out means saying a word out loud, so its sound is used, not its spelling

parts.note: excessively means too much; the word is spelt by its sound

explanation.surface: A family bans one member from speaking because they are far too blunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outspoken' looks like a description of a rude relative, but it says to hear TOO as TU.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantu is a large group of related languages spoken across central and southern Africa, including Swahili, Zulu and Xhosa.

clue.text: Needs, somehow, to insert line, tricky without stopping

indicators.note: inserting puts something inside, so one piece goes into the other
somehow means in some unspecified way, so these letters are put in some other order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange
L is the abbreviation for line
tricky and sly both mean cunning

explanation.surface: A writer must find a way to slip in an awkward line without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it is the raw letters; the line goes inside them after rearranging, and the tricky part comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Endlessly is an adverb meaning on and on with no end, which is the same as continuing with no pause.

clue.text: Staggered — so getting teeth knocked out, possibly?

definitions.note: a whimsical literal reading: smacked in the gob, the past participle standing for the event
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally and playfully: hit in the mouth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gob' is British slang for mouth, so the word taken literally means punched in the mouth; 'possibly' warns that the second reading is a joke. 'Staggered' could suggest reeling from a blow, which ties the halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobsmacked is British slang for astounded, the way one is staggered by shocking news.

clue.text: Beauty smuggling a gun, short piece

indicators.note: smuggled goods are hidden inside something, so one piece is concealed within another

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
taken as written
gat is old American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: A glamorous woman smuggles a handgun, perhaps a short piece, past the guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short piece' looks like a small gun, which suits the smuggling scene, but it is a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a short, light piece of music, usually for piano, such as Beethoven's Für Elise.

clue.text: Superior type seems noisome and obviously bourgeois, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.note: the opening letter
the opening letter
the opening letter
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone who thinks themselves superior comes across as unpleasant and plainly middle-class.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' is skipped: its initial would spoil the word, and it serves only as joinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob looks down on others, regarding themselves as socially or culturally superior, hence a superior type.

clue.text: Squeeze bone dry, if soused

indicators.note: soused means drunk, and a drunk staggers about, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Instructions for wringing something out until it is completely dry, unless it has been soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeeze' looks like an instruction to wring, but it is a noun, the slang for a romantic partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Main squeeze is informal for a sweetheart, so a squeeze can be someone's boyfriend.

clue.text: Can, a container of liquid drunk by bird

indicators.note: what is drunk goes inside the drinker, so one piece is taken into another

parts.note: a lory is a small brightly coloured parrot
taken as written
a vat is a large tank for liquids

explanation.surface: A bird drinks from a can or some other vessel holding liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' sits first as if it were a tin or the verb, but it is American slang for the toilet. The bird is a parrot, not the usual tern or emu.
explanation.definitionFit: The can is slang for a toilet, the room or fixture also called a lavatory.

clue.text: Old soldier on back in agony: stretcher found?

indicators.note: in an across answer, sitting on something means coming after it, so the first-named pieces go to the end
the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter
O is the abbreviation for old
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A veteran lies on his back in pain, waiting for a stretcher to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene makes 'stretcher' a medical carrier, but it is someone who stretches. Y, then O + GI placed on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A yogi practises yoga, whose postures involve a great deal of stretching, so a yogi is a stretcher in a playful sense.

clue.text: Weakness — old empire builder quick to conceal it

parts.note: the Inca built a great empire in the Andes

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one piece is tucked within another

parts.note: pacy means fast
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ageing empire builder quickly hides a weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: INCA, then PACY hiding IT. The 'old empire builder' is a people, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Incapacity is a lack of strength or ability to do something, which is a form of weakness.

clue.text: Rallying mid-morning? Not quite

definitions.note: a gerund naming an activity stands for the game in which that activity is central, a definition by example

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: around ten o'clock in the morning, 'ten-ish'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a rally takes place in the middle of the morning, and is told not exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rallying' suggests recovering or gathering supporters, but it is exchanging shots. TENNISH means at about ten; cut short it gives TENNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a rally is a sequence of shots returned back and forth, so rallying is the essence of the game.

clue.text: Monarch in clothes, striking

indicators.note: to clothe is to wrap around, so one piece covers the other

parts.note: in cricket the side that is in is batting
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A dressed-up king or queen cuts a striking figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in clothes' reads as 'dressed', but 'in' is the wordplay and 'clothes' the verb: in cricket, the team that is in is batting, and BATTING clothes ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Battering means hitting repeatedly and hard, so it is a form of striking.

clue.text: Lowest degree, like that

parts.note: a Bachelor of Arts, a university degree
Latin 'thus', printed to show a quotation is as written

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the lowest qualification, saying it is just like that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowest degree' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Lowest'; the degree is BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic describes the most elementary level, as in a basic wage, the bottom rung before anything extra.

clue.text: Old firefighter in commercial broadcast

parts.note: an advertisement
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A retired firefighter appears in a TV advert.
explanation.walkthrough: The firefighter is Red Adair, the American famous for putting out oil-well fires, so not someone from a local fire station.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul 'Red' Adair, who died in 2004, made his name capping blazing oil wells around the world.

clue.text: Back with vitality in abundance

parts.note: back in time, as in 'years back'
go is energy and drive

explanation.surface: Someone is back on form with plenty of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a return, but it means in the past, as in 'two years back'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gogo, from French, means galore or in plentiful supply, as in 'wine a gogo'.

clue.text: Gag vacuously lame, considering skirting round it?

indicators.note: to skirt round something is to go round its edge, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: both mean given that, as a conjunction

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word is emptied and only its outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A comic weighs whether to dodge a joke that falls flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' wants to be a joke, which the 'lame' surface supports, but it is the verb meaning to stop someone talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag someone is to stop them speaking, literally with a cloth or by order, so to silence them.

clue.text: A set of books inspired by remarkable island capital

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is drawn inside another

parts.note: as in 'that was some catch'
taken as written
the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A remarkable book series is said to have been inspired by an island capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' gives SOME in its informal sense, as in 'that was some party'.
explanation.definitionFit: São Tomé is the capital of São Tomé and Príncipe, an island nation in the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Dark liquid drunk by Osage leader, native American bottles

indicators.note: to bottle is to enclose in a vessel, so one piece holds the rest inside

parts.note: the Cree are a First Nations people of Canada

indicators.note: by means beside, and here the second-named piece stands in front of the first
a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A drunk, the head of the Osage tribe and a Native American with bottles of dark liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a verb about the dark liquid, but it is a noun for a drunkard. 'Osage leader' is just one letter; the Osage are a Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is a dark oily distillate of tar, painted on fences and timber as a preservative.

clue.text: Promise I've given? I don't believe it!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pledge someone has made
second meaning: an exclamation of astonishment

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a promise met with disbelief; the answer read plainly is the pledge you gave, and as an exclamation it expresses surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving your word is making a promise, and 'my word!' is an old-fashioned cry of amazement.
